title: Geometric specialization slices of the vanishing topos
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring (a local principal ideal domain of dimension one), $B=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $f:T\to B$ a finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring annihilated by an integer invertible on $B$, and $L\in D^b(T_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$. Choose a geometric closed point $\bar b$ [def-weil-geometric-point] of $B$, its strict localization $B_{(\bar b)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and a geometric generic point $\bar t\to B_{(\bar b)}$ with its specialization to $\bar b$. Put $T_{(\bar b)}=T\times_BB_{(\bar b)}$, $T_{\bar b}=T\times_B\bar b$, $T_{\bar t}=T_{(\bar b)}\times_{B_{(\bar b)}}\bar t$, and let $i:T_{\bar b}\to T_{(\bar b)}$, $j:T_{\bar t}\to T_{(\bar b)}$ be the natural maps. The specialization defines a geometric morphism $e_f:(T_{\bar b})_{\mathrm{Et}}\to V_f$, where $V_f$ and $R\Psi_f$ are as in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$e_f^*R\Psi_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*Rj_*(L|_{T_{\bar t}}).$$
For any $B$-morphism $h:T'\to T$, with induced $v:V_{f'}\to V_f$ and $h_{\bar b}:T'_{\bar b}\to T_{\bar b}$, this isomorphism identifies the pullback of the ordinary comparison $v^*R\Psi_fL\to R\Psi_{f'}h^*L$ with the ordinary comparison for $i^*Rj_*$ induced by $h$. It also identifies the restriction of the lax tensor map of $R\Psi_f$ with the lax tensor map of $i^*Rj_*$, using the canonical derived tensor comparison for inverse image. Neither compatibility asserts that the individual ordinary or tensor comparison is invertible.
